diagnostics.message: time_sleep.wait_30_seconds only gates on aws_iam_role.splunk_integration, so it does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration to be attached to that role. The permission policy is a sibling of the sleep (both depend only on the role), so the 30s IAM-readiness delay can elapse before the role actually carries its permissions — and signalfx_aws_integration.integration (which depends on this sleep) can then be created against a role that Splunk cannot yet use. The sleep should also depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration so the delay covers the full role setup.

time_sleep.wait_30_seconds does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy, so the metric-streams policy (which grants iam:PassRole and cloudwatch:*MetricStream permissions) is not ordered before the delay finishes. Because signalfx_aws_integration.integration uses use_metric_streams_sync/enable_aws_usage and depends on this sleep, Splunk can attempt to set up metric streams while the role still lacks those permissions, hitting the manual-intervention bad state the sleep is meant to prevent. The sleep should also depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy.
